title: Determinant weights of a finite tensor power
statement:
Let $\mathcal F_0$ be a nonzero lisse Weil sheaf with
semisimple geometric
representation on a normal geometrically connected curve $X_0$, and let
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ be its determinant weights, counted with
multiplicity in [def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset]. For every
$k\ge1$, every Jordan–Holder constituent of the tensor power
$\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ (constituents and tensor products of Weil
representations as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]) has
determinant weight

$$
\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}
$$

for some indices $i_1,\ldots,i_k$, and every such sum occurs for at
least one constituent. In particular, if $\beta=\max_i\alpha_i$, the
largest determinant weight of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ is
$k\beta$.

proof.text: By [lem-mg-composition-series-exists], choose a composition series of the Weil representation of $\mathcal F_0$ in the sense of [def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors $A_1,\ldots,A_n$. By [lem-mg-jordan-holder], the factors are independent of the chosen series up to permutation and isomorphism with multiplicity. The definition of the determinantal-weight multiset therefore lets us reindex so that $\alpha_i=\dw_\iota(A_i)$ for every $i$. By [lem-rp-determinant-weights-agree], each $A_i$ has finite geometric determinant and $\dw_\iota(A_i)=\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(A_i)$. The same lemma gives finite geometric determinant and equality of the two weight notions for every nonzero Jordan--Hölder constituent of every tensor power, since by the exact tensor equivalence [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] between lisse Weil sheaves on $X_0$ and Weil representations, every tensor power of the Weil representation of $\mathcal F_0$ and every subquotient of it is the Weil representation of a lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$, so each such constituent is a nonzero (irreducible) lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$.

We prove by induction on $k\ge 1$ the two assertions that every constituent of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ has weight equal to a sum of $k$ of the $\alpha_i$, and that every such sum occurs. For $k=1$, the constituents are exactly the factors $A_i$ of the chosen composition series by [lem-mg-jordan-holder] and [def-real-weil-representation-operations], and their weights are $\alpha_i$ by the preceding identification. Thus both assertions hold in the base case.

Assume the assertions for $k-1\ge1$. Write $\mathcal V_0=\mathcal F_0^{\otimes(k-1)}$ and $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal F_0$. The recursive tensor action of [def-real-weil-representation-operations] identifies their tensor product with $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$. Tensoring nonzero vectors gives a nonzero tensor: choose linear functionals taking value $1$ on each vector, whose tensor evaluates it to $1$. Thus every positive tensor power is nonzero. The tensor matrix coefficients are products of the original continuous coefficients, so these remain finite-dimensional Weil representations, continuous on the geometric subgroup; by the exact tensor equivalence [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] they are the Weil representations of the nonzero lisse Weil sheaves $\mathcal V_0$ and $\mathcal E_0$ on $X_0$, whose tensor product is the lisse Weil sheaf with Weil representation that of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$. By [lem-mg-composition-series-exists], choose composition series whose factors are the Jordan--Hölder constituents of $\mathcal V_0$ and the factors $A_j$ of $\mathcal E_0$. All these factors and all constituents of the tensor product have finite geometric determinant by Step 1. Apply [prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor] with $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$. It says that every constituent $Q$ of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ has $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(Q)=\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(V_i)+\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(A_j)$ for some constituent $V_i$ of $\mathcal V_0$ and some $j$. Using Step 1 and the induction hypothesis gives $\dw_\iota(Q)=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_{k-1}}+\alpha_j$.

Conversely, let $\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ be any sum. By the induction hypothesis, the first $k-1$ terms occur as the weight of some constituent $V_i$ of $\mathcal V_0$. The converse clause of [prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor] then supplies a constituent of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ of weight $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(V_i)+\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(A_{i_k})=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$, using Step 1 for the final equality. Hence the induction closes. If $\beta=\max_i\alpha_i$, every occurring sum is at most $k\beta$, while choosing an index with $\alpha_i=\beta$ in every position gives the occurring sum $k\beta$; therefore the largest determinant weight is $k\beta$.
